Other Ways to Pledge

There are several ways to support the VMI Foundation or the VMI Keydet Club through an estate plan or other planned gift.

Bequests in a Will or TrustLeave a specific dollar amount, personal property, real estate, or a percentage of your estate to VMI.
Beneficiary DesignationsName VMI as a primary or contingent beneficiary on an IRA, 401(k), 403(b), bank account, investment account, or life insurance policy.
Charitable Remainder Trusts or “Give It Twice” TrustsEstablish a trust that provides income to a spouse or children for life or for a set period, with the remaining balance later transferred to VMI.
Charitable Gift AnnuitiesMake a gift in exchange for fixed lifetime payments for one or two people, with the remaining funds later supporting VMI.
Donor Advised FundsContribute to a donor advised fund, receive an immediate tax deduction, and recommend future gifts to VMI.
Charitable EndowmentsCreate an endowed fund through a will or trust. The principal is invested, and annual income supports a chosen area of VMI.

Planned gifts may qualify donors for membership in the Legacy Society, which includes invitations to special events, recognition in publications, and a Legacy Pin.

House Mountain Challenge

Thursday, November 12, 2026 · 10:00 a.m.–4:45 p.m. EST (target schedule)

A VMI Class of 2001 25th Reunion hike recognizing 25 years of brotherhood, leadership, accomplishments, and remembrance. The route is approximately 8.9–10.4 miles, depending on the route, with approximately 3,000 feet of elevation gain. Expect strenuous, steep, rocky terrain.

Two summits: Big House Mountain (Goat Point Overlook) and Little House Mountain (Valley Overlook), with views of the Allegheny Ranges and Shenandoah Valley.

Target Timeline

10:00 a.m. — StartDepart from Saddle Ridge Road Parking Lot
11:15 a.m. — Saddle Meadow2.5 miles; quick break by the shelter
11:25 a.m. — Climb Big House MountainSteep, rocky ascent from the Saddle
12:15 p.m. — Summit 1: Goat Point Overlook3.8 miles; lunch and panoramic views
12:45 p.m. — DescendReturn toward the meadow over loose rock fields
1:30 p.m. — Return to Saddle5.1 miles; continue northeast toward Little House Mountain
2:30 p.m. — Summit 2: Little House Overlook6.5 miles; valley views
3:00 p.m. — Descend7.9 miles; switchbacks toward the Saddle
3:45 p.m. — Final stretchDescend the main access road
4:45 p.m. — Finish10.4 miles; return to vehicles before dusk

Parking & Logistics

Trailhead: House Mountain Parking Area (Saddle Ridge Road), Lexington, VA 24450. Park only in the designated gravel lot. Do not park on road shoulders or block access. Parking is limited; carpool when possible.

What to Pack & Wear

Sturdy high-top hiking boots, trekking poles, 2.5–3 liters of water, packed lunch and high-energy snacks, long pants and tall socks, layered clothing, and an offline or printed trail map. Cell service may be unreliable. Bring plenty of water and ibuprofen as noted in the event graphic.

Featured Brother Rats

Class of 2001 spotlight

Charlie Bunting

What are you doing now?I'm living in Sleepy Hollow, NY, with my wife, Lindsey; our son, Cassius, who's almost 2; and our dog, Yoda. I run a small executive search firm with a fellow former DIA colleague, helping build the leadership teams of manufacturing and production companies in the national security space. Outside of work, I volunteer with Merging Vets and Players and the Defense Intelligence Memorial Foundation. More than anything, I feel incredibly lucky to be a dad, and I try to spend as much time as I can with my parents in Rhode Island. I'm also trying to get back in the water to spearfish, though naptime doesn't leave me much time to get away.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMIMy biggest takeaway from VMI is how lucky we are to have our Brother Rats—to stand by each other and stay friends all these years later. The older I get, the more I realize how rare and important that is.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion?I can't wait to see everyone and introduce my little guy, Cashie B! I'm also excited for the class to meet the new Supe. He reminds me a lot of my dad, and he's an evangelist for the Corps of Cadets.

Previously Featured Brother Rats

Class of 2001 spotlight archive

Matt Meyers

CEO, B.E. Meyers & Co.

What are you doing now? CEO of B.E. Meyers & Co. in Redmond, Washington, a defense technology manufacturer specializing in combat-proven laser systems for U.S. Special Operations Command and other services within the U.S. Department of War, as well as law enforcement and international defense and aerospace customers. “American Made Precision Laser Death Rays” is the family business, now in its 52nd year.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMI The VMI network is truly incredible and surpasses every other service out there because of all the different paths people choose after they graduate. It is amazing to see where classmates go and the things they discover.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion? I have only been back briefly a few times, but I am interested to see Lexington and what has changed and what has stayed the same.

Kevin Consedine

Commander, Corpus Christi Army Depot

What are you doing now? I am currently serving as the Commander of Corpus Christi Army Depot, where I lead the Army's premier helicopter maintenance and sustainment organization. After 26 years in Army Aviation, I am fortunate to maintain my flight status and continue flying helicopters, which keeps me connected to the profession and Soldiers who first inspired me to serve.

As I prepare to retire from the Army next year, I am beginning to look toward a second career focused on the intersection of national security, public policy, and the industrial base. Outside of work, my wife, Meagan, and I stay busy raising our two teenagers. Much of our free time is spent traveling for our son's college soccer recruiting journey and our daughter's theater aspirations. I have also enjoyed writing on defense and industrial base issues for publications such as War on the Rocks and RealClearDefense.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMI I do not have a single defining memory from VMI that stands above the rest. Instead, what has stayed with me is the foundation the Institute provided. VMI taught us that leadership begins with character and that integrity, accountability, and service to something greater than yourself are daily expectations.

Looking back 25 years later, I appreciate even more how unique that education was. The environment challenged us to develop resilience, humility, and the ability to lead under pressure. Those lessons have only become more relevant throughout my Army career, and I suspect they are even more valuable today than when we graduated.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion? I am looking forward to reconnecting with classmates and hearing everyone's stories. We have all taken very different paths over the past 25 years, and I am excited to learn where life has taken everyone, professionally and personally. I am also looking forward to walking post again and remembering the friendships and shared experiences that continue to connect us.

Carl Haas

Assistant Men's Lacrosse Coach, Frostburg State University

What are you doing now?

I am an Assistant Men's Lacrosse Coach at Frostburg State in Maryland. I have been a college coach for 23 years and have been all over on this journey. I met my wife, Judy, while coaching at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. We married in 2015 and have three kids. I have always been into video games, but with three kids and my work schedule, I get one hobby, and it is still playing video games.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMI

VMI taught me how to grow, adapt, overcome obstacles, and find a way to get something done. It was the right place for me, and I loved my time at VMI.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion?

I think it is that feeling of slipping right back into conversations and friendships that pick up as if no time had gone by. We will rehash some of the same stories, but it is about feeling connected to people I depended on, looked up to, and who helped me grow.

The Institute did a lot of molding, but the people to my left and right did more. I cannot wait to see you all again.

Brandon Bowman

Commander, Jacksonville District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers

I am in my final year as Commander of the Jacksonville District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The district is currently in its 26th year of restoring the Everglades, the largest ecosystem restoration project in the known galaxy. Beyond the Everglades, we oversee 28 coastal storm risk management projects, manage water levels in Lake Okeechobee, and maintain Florida's deep-water harbors.

Next summer, I will most likely retire from the Army and move back to Pennsylvania. My wife and I recently purchased an old mill house built in 1750 that was once owned by my great-great-grandparents. It is only about a mile and a half from where I grew up and where my parents still live.

Since we are close to Orlando, we have been spending long weekends at Disney World and Universal Studios. In my free time, I work on a 1962 TVR Grantura and a 1967 Land Rover Series IIA. I also recently bought a pinball machine, which has turned out to be one of the best dumb purchases I have ever made.

VMI reflection

One of my favorite memories is hearing the Christmas carols played after Taps during the holiday season. The image that stays with me is walking through the stoops after dark, seeing the lights glowing in barracks, and watching cadets move through Jackson Arch.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion?

Despite multiple deployments and a busy Army career, I have never missed a class reunion, and I hope to keep that streak alive. It is always great to see everyone again, catch up on where life has taken us, and discover just how much older, and in many cases wider, we have all become.

John (Koub) Koubaroulis

What are you doing now?

After graduating VMI, I served in the U.S. Army and U.S. Air Force Reserve as an Intelligence Officer. I served for 11 months in Iraq with the Army’s first Stryker Brigade Combat Team leading a Shadow TUAV platoon. Later, I had a storied career at the FBI. Since then, and for 14 years, I’ve been teaching English Language Arts (ELA) and English as a Second Language (ESL) online, in the classroom, and abroad. I’ve taught in South Korea and Saudi Arabia. Most recently, I’ve been teaching middle school ELA at a charter school in Washington, D.C. and adult immigrants from Florida ESL online.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMI

VMI gave me the leadership skills to succeed in the military and government. Had I not attended VMI, I would not be where I am today.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion?

I’m looking forward to seeing all of my roommates and sharing unforgettable moments together!
